questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

By whom was this done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Who did this?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The** subject **of the **Passive Voice** is changed into the **object **of the **Active Voice**. Also, the **object **of the **Passive Voice** is changed into the **subject **of the **Active Voice**.
 
• The **removal **of the** helping verb** and the preposition** 'by'** is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.
 
• In Active voice (look at the options), it should be in **interrogative form**. These are “wh” questions that don’t take “yes” or “no” as an answer.
 
• **“By whom?” **is changed into **“Who”** while transforming from Passive to Active.
 
• For example:
 
 
• By whom were you taught Math?
 
• Who taught you Math? (Active)
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context,** 'By whom'** should be changed to **'Who'**.
 
• The sentence in the Passive voice is in **Simple Past Tense **(denoted by 'was). So, the sentence in the Active voice should be in **Simple Past Tense **(denoted by 'did').
 
• The options except **(4)** don’t follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***Who did this?.***

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Rohit said, “The board game is mine.”

options.text: Rohit said that the board game was his.
Rohit said that the board game was me.
Rohit said that he was the board game.
Rohit said that the board game were hers.

questions.solution:
The correct option is: **Rohit said that the board game was his**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When converting direct speech to reported speech, the tense typically shifts back.
 
• Hence **"is" **(Present tense) becomes** "was" **(Past tense) in reported speech.
 
• **Pronouns** also change according to the speaker and context. **"Mine"** changes to** "his"** when reporting Rohit's speech.
 
• The structure "Rohit said that..." is used to introduce the reported speech, maintaining the meaning of the original statement while adhering to grammatical norms for reported speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is- ***Rohit said that the board game was his*.**

• For example: Rohit **cut down** fatty food recently.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

There are more than two million / job-seekers who are already / completed their fitness test / for the post since 2020.

options.text: There are more than two million

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **job-seekers who are already**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The segment **"completed their fitness test"** lacks an **auxiliary verb** to link the subject **"job-seekers"** with the past participle **"completed."**
 
• The correct construction should involve the use of** "have"** to form the present perfect tense, as in **"have completed their fitness test."**
 
• The** present perfect tense **is used because the action of completing the fitness test has relevance to the present moment, especially considering "since 2020."
 
 
• For example: I **have** done all my homework.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, incorporating **"have"** correctly indicates that the job-seekers completed their fitness test at some point in the past, with implications for the present (since 2020).

Therefore, the correct answer is- *There are more than two million job-seekers who **have** already completed their fitness test for the post since 2020.*

questions.question: What is the primary inference that can be made by reading this passage?

options.text: Anxiety can be defeated by a positive attitude and productive practices.

• The passage does not mention FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out) as a cause of anxiety, making option 3 irrelevant.
 
• While the passage acknowledges anxiety as a significant concern, it does not suggest that anxiety is insurmountable or that it cannot be managed individually, making option 4 incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***Anxiety can be defeated by a positive attitude and productive practices.***

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***Fear of Missing Out.***
